about: The backup (docs/plan.md slice 17; tasks.md call 5, decided 2026-10-02): the app's store splits in two. The pump rows (the pumps the app keeps: id, source, start in unix ms, seconds, title, moves with their seconds, and since slice 33 an app pump's kind (a key of contract/kinds.json, quick for the Quick pump or, since slice 36, move for a move started from a step's card or a move's window) and the game link whose finish offered it (a key of contract/links.json), and since 2026-10-12 a catch-up's move its typed set (the `set` its `pump_done` carries) when the player saved a count on it, and since 2026-10-26 the move Swap put in its place on its Ready view (the `ran` its `pump_done` carries, `down` and all), so a catch-up waiting for the helper still pays as the move that ran wherever it is restored and the Log names that move, and since 2026-10-16 a pump after a game on the phone its game (the game's own name, at most 40 Unicode scalars), the matches the player answered and the session's minutes (docs/phone-games.md B4; never the name in a row, the helper, the game's save or any telemetry), each written only when present, so an older file reads as before, and since slice 44 the card of a game pump's move the wrist ran (`<game pump id>/<slot>`, source watch, the title of a game pump of one move) its one move (contract/companion-api.yaml RelayedPump.gameMove), where a card kept before it, or from an older watch, has none, and since its last review (2026-10-17) each move of a game pump the phone ran (source phone, under the game pump's id) its slot in the game's pump (the OfferedMove.slot it ran as, the slot its move row has, which contract/fixtures/history.json `log` reads to list it until that row comes) and beside it its own go (start_ms, unix ms: the move's first go on the phone, at which `log` lists it), none on any other pump's move or on one kept before; the app's own rows and the kept game rows in the addon's grammar; the kept sheets; since 2026-10-30 the game's characters as a helper's GET /v1/sheet last served them (game.characters, written only when there are any); the free mode's settings, since 2026-10-30 with their body fields' times (body, the Body of POST /v1/body in contract/companion-api.yaml, written only when a field has one)) go into the device backup and the backup file; the body notes (heart rate and the heart-rate proofs, pain rows, the check-in's answers, every row stopped or banked for pain or felt unwell, and a pump's unwell mark) stay out of both, on the device (since slice 26 the app's own pain, check-in and unwell rows also go to the paired helper and the game's save, and "Start over in the app" keeps its pain rows and, since slice 30, its focus rows (kind 16: one focus for the account), since 2026-10-08 its clear rows (kind 17) and, since slice 44, its correction and load rows (kinds 7 and 18), each whatever its time: `imports`' floor case).`split` is the rule for a row: a body note when its kind is pain (9) or checkin (12), or a move, level-up or pump row (kinds 1-6) whose reason (flags bits 0-2) is 3, pain, or 4, felt unwell. `book` is the file a store makes (`Backup.project`): its pumps by start then id without peak_bpm, rise_bpm, verdict and unwell, less a pump that ran nothing (no move and no second: only a felt-unwell stop keeps one, so it would tell of the stop), its rows and kept game rows without the body notes (a game row without hr_verdict, hr_peak and hr_delta), its sheets, its characters each with a sheet and without its sheet's felt-unwell days (lk) and the owed moves its rider gates hold back (held, ns.OwedHeld, a pain flag among the gates), so no trace of a body note goes with them, the oldest left out past 512000 bytes of their JSON (Backup.carried), and its settings with their times. `imports` take files into a store in turn (`Backup.restore`): a pump by its id (the store's own stays, with its heart rate; a store's pumps are by start, then id), rows as the addon merges a mirror (DB.lua ns.MergeMirror): a row's identity is its text, a game row's its fields without the proof, counted by copies, so a row both hold is kept once and two alike in one log stay two; each log keeps its order and the two interleave by time (a row that repeats an older time, a correction or a paid row, stays after the rows written before it), the store's row first within a second; sheets by their character and their JSON with sorted keys, the file's new ones after the store's; each character the newer of the store's and the file's by its sheet's `at` (the store's at a tie: Backup.newest), a character known by its guid (by its place in the addon's list where it has none), at the place the store gives it, one new to the store at its own place or, where another character holds that place, the first after every other; the file's settings whole, with their times, into a store with no settings of its own, whatever history it holds, and since 2026-10-30 into a store with its own the file's body field by field, each that changed at or after the store's own taking the file's value and time (BodyExchange.take, as POST /v1/body merges), the place (equipment, floor, space, quiet) staying the store's, while a file without times (an older one) brings none of its settings (the Body switches are filters a restore must not drop without a word; the app says when it kept its own). So a second import of the same file changes nothing and two files with rows in common keep each row once. A case's `change` is what its last file brought, for the words the player reads (`Backup.change`): the pumps, the moves they hold (each pump's moves; the count the words name since 2026-10-27) and the rows (the app's and the game's) that came, `other` when sheets, characters or settings came, and `kept_settings` when the file carried other settings of which none came because the store has its own (a file without times; since 2026-10-30 also one whose every field the store changed later, its place aside). `rows` pins the merge order. `refuse` names the files a reader refuses whole. QuestPumpCore's and the Android core's Backup implement every case; the iPhone and Android apps read each other's files, and a file the desktop app made (device computer, slice 35).

book.about: a phone's store and the file it makes: the free pump stopped for felt unwell before a move stays out (it ran nothing, so it would tell only of the stop), the watch's own pump (no move, but its seconds) stays without its heart rate, the pending catch-up as pending, the app pump a Lichess finish offered with its kind and its link, the push-up the wrist ran in the game pump offered at 1790130000 (its card, slot 0, with its move since slice 44: contract/companion-api.yaml RelayedPump.gameMove) as one move without its heart rate, the chair squat and the plank the phone ran in phone-only mode in the game pump offered at 1790140000 with their targets, their slots in the game's pump and their own goes (since slice 44's last review) and without its heart rate, the app pump after 52 minutes of Wild Rift on the phone with its kind, its game, its matches and its minutes (its title the book's, no name in it); the pain flag, the check-in, the unwell stop, the game's pain flag and unwell stop stay out; the game's pump row loses its proof

imports.about: a backup file made on the iPhone restores on a fresh install: its pumps, rows, kept game rows and sheets, and the settings of the free mode, none of its body notes
a second import of the same file changes nothing
two files with rows in common, the older first: every row once, the newer pump added
the same two files the other way round: the same store
into a phone with settings of its own but no history yet: the file's history comes in, the phone's settings stay
into a phone that paired first (the game's rows, no settings of its own): the file's settings come in with its history, the Body switches among them
a file an Android phone made, into a fresh install

a file the desktop app made (device computer, slice 35), into a fresh install: its rows are the computer's (bit 12, the text a phone keeps the helper's copy of them in, so a phone that took them from the helper keeps each once), read as any file's
the same sheets written with their keys in another order (another app's encoder) are kept once

into a phone with history of its own (another platform's file): its pumps keep their heart rate, its pain rows and its free mode's settings stay, a pump both hold stays the phone's, the file's rows interleave by time

the floor (slice 44): Start over in the app keeps the correction and load rows from before it (kinds 7 and 18) whatever their time, as it keeps the pain, focus and clear rows. A correction carries the time of the set it names, so the phone's corrections of two game sets, made after its Start over, are dated before it: the wall push-ups typed as 45 and corrected to 15 (round 1), and the goblet squat's 16 kg corrected to 12 kg with its 12 reps kept (its load row, then its correction row, both round 1). They stay, since the game's sets stay (only the app's own history starts again); until slice 44 the floor dropped them. The file, made before the Start over, brings the app's own pump, set, focus and clear rows of before it: the pump and the set go, the focus and the clear row stay, and so does the set's own load row (round 0), which names a set the app's fold no longer holds and changes nothing there. Backup.Floor in both cores, questpump-core's app_rows::after_start_over and tools/apppump.lua's FLOOR_KEEPS keep the same kinds

rows.about: the logs interleave by time, the kept row first where two are of one second
a row both logs hold is kept once
two rows alike in one log (the same second) stay two
a row that repeats an older time stays after the rows written before it in its own log
